svg.title: How Apache, HAProxy, Varnish, and nginx combine workers and readiness
svg.desc: Apache event MPM parks idle keep-alive sockets and hands active work to threads. HAProxy uses event-driven workers. Varnish combines worker threads for active work with a waiter for idle connections. Nginx uses worker processes with event loops and optional helper threads.

g.text: Different servers converge on the same division of labour
A readiness mechanism holds waiting sockets; a bounded set of workers performs useful work.
Apache event MPM
processes contain listener/event handling + worker threads
waiting:
idle keep-alive sockets parked by event logic
working:
requests run on worker threads
Avoids dedicating a worker thread to an idle keep-alive wait.
HAProxy
event-driven processing with platform-specific pollers
waiting:
readiness events for client and upstream sockets
working:
proxy, balance, buffer, reuse upstream connections
Its role is a proxy/load balancer, not an application runtime.
Varnish
HTTP caching reverse proxy with thread pools and waiters
waiting:
idle client/backend FDs held by a waiter
working:
active requests use threads from bounded pools
Caching can avoid an origin request entirely.
nginx
master manages worker processes; workers run event loops
waiting:
many connections per worker readiness loop
working:
HTTP/proxy work; optional threads for blocking file I/O
sendfile can avoid copying static payload through user space.
Products differ in details; the reusable idea is separate waiting from working.
